newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Bank Portugal to revise 96 growth forecast -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Bank Portugal to revise 96 growth forecast -- paper.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal should revise its 1996 economic growth forecast upwards in its third quarter report to be published soon, the Expresso weekly reported.

The newspaper quoted central bank governor Antonio De Sousa as saying that given the progress of the German economy, Portugal's main export market, "it is natural that (Portuguese) growth should stand in the upper half of between 1.75 and 2.75 percent".
The newspaper said the Bank of Portugal was expected to narrow its growth forecast for 1996 to between 2.25 and 2.75 percent from its earlier projection of 1.75 to 2.75 percent.
De Sousa told Expresso that he expected economic growth in Portugal next year to be equal to or better than in 1996.
"The second half (this year) is better than the first half and next year should maintain this trend," he said. "Real salaries should increase next year as much as or slightly less than in 1996."
The 1997 public sector wage talks between the Socialist government and trade union groups start on Wednesday.
De Sousa told Expresso he believed union wage demands were too high and that a one percent differential above inflation should be the maximum acceptable level.
Public-sector unions are demanding wage increases of between 4.5 and 7.0 for 1997. The government has forecast inflation of between 2.25 and 2.50 percent for next year.
De Sousa said he was optimistic that Portugal would meet convergence criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"Right now we have not met any of the convergence criteria formally, but we are very close to all of them," he said.
He said the 1998 budget to be presented next year would be crucial to meeting the targets.
"The probability of meeting the convergence criteria is very good with a budget that should hit the three percent (of gross domestic product) budget deficit goal," he said.
The government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres plans to present its 1997 budget proposals to parliament on October 15. Analysts expect the budget to be passed easily.
De Sousa ruled out the possibility of Portugal selling some of its gold reserves to help it meet the convergence criteria.
"The Bank of Portugal is not thinking of selling gold at this time," he said. "There has been no suggestion from the government to this effect," he added.
